# Where this goes

## Splitting it up

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Censoring was the first piece. It is now one package among several,
  all of them wrappers over `Distributions.jl`
- `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` does the sum of independent delays, with
  closed forms where they exist and the same fixed node quadrature
  where they do not, plus differences, products and ratios
- `DistributionsInference.jl` turns any of them into a
  `LogDensityProblems` problem, so the sampler stops being the
  package's choice
- Neither of those two packages knows the other exists. The example on
  the right works because both of them speak `Distributions.jl`
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
using CensoredDistributions
using ConvolvedDistributions, Distributions

incubation = Gamma(2.0, 1.0)
reporting = LogNormal(1.0, 0.5)

d = convolved(incubation, reporting)
observed = double_interval_censored(
    d; upper = 15, interval = 1
)

cdf(observed, 5.0)   # 0.4561
```
:::
::::

## Compound distributions

- The generation time is the delay between one infection and the next.
  It is never observed, so it is inferred through the serial interval
  and the incubation period
- That is a convolution, a difference and a censoring adjustment
  stacked on each other, which is exactly what these packages are for
- `GenerationTime.jl` is currently an empty repository. That is the
  honest state of it
- Next is a composed Julia version of `epidist`, our R package for
  delay estimation, with Turing submodels for partially pooled and
  flexible delays

::: {.attribution}
Open issue #749 says the joint fit is too slow, because reverse mode
autodiff through `cdf(Convolved(...))` costs too much per leapfrog step.
:::

## What I would use today

- If you estimate delays in R, use `primarycensored`. It works, it is on
  CRAN, and there are packages built on top of it
- If you are writing a model in Julia, the composition is worth more
  than the package. Any distribution, any sampler, no integer tables
- Multiple dispatch removed a class of bug that R and Stan could only
  write a test for
- It did not remove the numerical problem. That moved to a list of
  which autodiff backends work

::: {.callout-important}
The composition is the reusable part. The package is only where the
censoring happens to live.
:::
